# Skein — full LLM context

Skein is a small HTML-first Web Components runtime for creative websites and interactive documents. It adds fine-grained reactivity, scoped lifecycle, keyed lists, conditions and ergonomic bindings while leaving rendering media native: HTML stays HTML, CSS stays CSS, SVG stays SVG and Canvas stays imperative Canvas.

Current public runtime version: 0.4.x.
Production/CDN entry: `skein.min.js`.
Readable source entry: `skein.js` + `runtime/` modules.
Bundle size: 21.4 kB raw, 6.1 kB gzip, 5.6 kB Brotli.
Dependencies: 0.
Repository: https://github.com/Pom4H/web-component
Website: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/
Playground: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/playground/

## Core philosophy

1. The browser is already the rendering engine. Do not introduce a virtual DOM.
2. Static content should remain static HTML. Skein binds only dynamic data.
3. SEO-critical content such as the value proposition, headings, links, product copy and structured information should normally be present in the original HTML response.
4. Skein currently has no SSR or hydration. If server-computed HTML is required, generate that HTML outside Skein and let Skein enhance the result.
5. Templates stay readable HTML. Expressions inside `{...}` are property paths, not arbitrary JavaScript expressions.
6. Put derived logic in `computed()` rather than embedding logic into markup.
7. Prefer native browser APIs over framework abstractions when the platform already provides the capability.
8. Keep the dependency count at zero in the core and official examples.

## Smallest app

```html
<!doctype html>

<click-count></click-count>

<template skein="click-count">
  <script>
    this.count = 0
    this.up = () => this.count++
  </script>

  <button @click={up}>clicked {count}</button>
</template>

<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Pom4H/web-component@main/skein.min.js">
</script>
```

No npm, CLI, bundler, config file or framework dev server is required. Pin a commit SHA instead of `@main` for reproducible production deployment.

## Larger project convention

A custom-element tag maps to an HTML component file by replacing hyphens with slashes:

```text
<counter-app> -> counter/app.html
<user-card>   -> user/card.html
```

A component file may contain `<script>`, markup and `<style>` in one file.

```html
<script>
  this.name = 'Ada'
  this.greeting = computed(() => `Hello ${this.name}`)
</script>

<h2>{greeting}</h2>

<style>
  h2 { text-wrap: balance; }
</style>
```

## State

Component scripts execute with `this` bound to a deep reactive Proxy.

```js
this.count = 0
this.count++
this.user = { name: 'Ada' }
this.user.name = 'Grace'
this.items = []
this.items.push({ id: 1, title: 'One' })
```

Application code should use ordinary JavaScript assignments. Do not expose signal `.get()` / `.set()` ceremony unless low-level primitives are intentionally required.

## Bindings

```html
<h1>Hello {user.name}</h1>
<div title="User {user.name}"></div>
<input .value={user.name}>
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
```

Also supported:

```html
<button onclick={save}>Save</button>
<button onclick="$.save(event)">Save</button>
```

`$` is component state exposed on rendered elements for inline browser handlers.

Context:

```html
<address in={user.address}>
  {city}, {street}
</address>
```

`in={...}` creates a lexical binding context. Lookup walks outward through parent contexts and then component state. An existing local property with value `undefined` still shadows an outer property of the same name.

## Lists

```html
<article for={projects} key={id}>
  <b>{index}. {title}</b>
  <input placeholder="DOM state survives reorder">
</article>
```

Use a stable `key={id}` when records have application identity. Without an explicit key, objects use object identity and primitive duplicates are disambiguated by occurrence.

List reconciliation is incremental: append creates only new views, removal disposes only removed views and reorder moves existing DOM nodes instead of recreating them. `index` and `$index` are reactive list locals. Do not replace keyed lists with full `innerHTML` rerenders.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={inspectorOpen}>
  <canvas></canvas>
</section>
```

A conditional branch owns a child reactive scope. When false, its effects, event listeners, nested scopes and DOM range are disposed together.

## Computed, effects and scheduling

```js
this.total = computed(() => this.price * this.quantity)

effect(() => {
  console.log(this.total)
})

batch(() => {
  this.x = 1
  this.y = 2
})
```

Computed values are lazy, cached and dependency-tracked. Synchronous writes are batched into a microtask. Render effects settle before user effects. Use `untrack(fn)` when reading reactive state without subscribing.

## Lifecycle and cleanup

Every component owns a root `Scope`; lists and branches create child scopes.

Prefer native AbortSignal integration:

```js
window.addEventListener('resize', this.measure, { signal: abortSignal })
fetch('/data.json', { signal: abortSignal })
```

For resources without AbortSignal support:

```js
const timer = setInterval(this.tick, 1000)
onCleanup(() => clearInterval(timer))
```

Disconnect pauses a component rather than permanently destroying it. Reconnection resumes dirty bindings. Permanent teardown is explicit with `host.dispose()` / element `dispose()`.

## Dynamic registration

```js
Skein.define('my-card', source)
```

`Skein.define()` registers source directly without a component-file fetch. If the tag already belongs to Skein, existing instances reload against the newly registered source. It refuses to take over a custom element defined outside Skein.

Automatic unknown-tag discovery is deferred by one task. This prevents a dynamic-import caller from racing with auto file loading before it can call `Skein.define()`.

## SEO and progressive enhancement

Skein currently has no SSR. This does not mean all page content should be client-rendered.

```html
<main>
  <h1>Creative websites with native HTML, CSS, SVG and Canvas.</h1>
  <p>Skein adds fine-grained reactive bindings without a virtual DOM or build step.</p>
  <a href="/pricing/">See pricing</a>

  <price-calculator></price-calculator>
</main>
```

The heading, paragraph and link are already present in the HTML response. Skein owns the interactive calculator. If the server must compute personalized/request-dependent HTML before delivery, use an external server or static-generation layer.

## Creative CSS pattern

Bind state into attributes or CSS custom properties and let CSS animate/layout:

```html
<article style="--x:{x}px" @pointermove={move}>
  <h1>Skein</h1>
</article>
```

Do not reproduce CSS interpolation, transitions, layout or keyframes in JavaScript unless necessary.

## SVG pattern

Keep the SVG tree native and bind only dynamic attributes:

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <circle cx={x} cy={y} r="4" />
</svg>
```

Do not convert SVG into a framework-specific object tree.

## Canvas pattern

Canvas normally retains an imperative render loop. Skein manages state, controls, ownership and cleanup rather than making each pixel declarative. Cancel animation frames in `onCleanup()`.

## Public component-script helpers

- `computed(fn)` — lazy cached derived value.
- `effect(fn)` — user effect scheduled after render work.
- `onCleanup(fn)` — deterministic teardown.
- `batch(fn)` — group synchronous writes.
- `signal(value)` — explicit low-level signal ref.
- `untrack(fn)` — non-reactive read.
- `host` — current `SkeinElement` instance.
- `abortSignal` — current scope-owned AbortSignal.

## Public browser/module API

The canonical namespace is `Skein` / `window.Skein`.

```js
Skein.name
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
Skein.element(tag)
Skein.stats
Skein.flush()
Skein.Signal
Skein.Computed
Skein.Effect
Skein.ReactiveState
Skein.Scope
Skein.Element
```

There are no pre-Skein compatibility globals or compatibility entry files.

## Runtime architecture

Readable source:

```text
skein.js
runtime/reactive.js
runtime/template.js
runtime/component.js
```

Production artifact:

```text
skein.min.js
```

`runtime/reactive.js` contains signals, computed refs, effects, batching, ownership scopes, the reactive Proxy and lexical BindingScope.

`runtime/template.js` compiles DOM templates once and creates specialized text, attribute, property, boolean, event, list and branch Parts.

`runtime/component.js` implements component loading, source compilation, `SkeinElement` lifecycle, helpers and registration.

Runtime invariants:
- no virtual DOM;
- no component-level rerender loop;
- templates compile once per component source;
- exact reactive reads drive exact parts;
- DOM parts skip identical commits;
- keyed list identity is preserved;
- scopes own effects and cleanup;
- render work runs before user effects;
- no core third-party dependency;
- production bundle semantics match readable source.

## Playground security

The official playground runs user/share code in a sandboxed iframe with `allow-scripts` only, without `allow-same-origin`. Runtime and component source are serialized safely into the isolated document; literal `<` is escaped before embedding inside the module script so component `</script>` tags cannot terminate the playground bootstrap script.

## Testing

Run:

```bash
node test/run.mjs
```

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and Chrome/Chromium (`CHROME_BIN` can be set explicitly). The runner uses Node built-ins and raw Chrome DevTools Protocol; do not add Playwright, Puppeteer, jsdom, Jest or Vitest merely for core tests.

Tests should cover reactive core behavior, browser bindings, keyed identity, reorder/disposal, scheduler batching, lifecycle/reconnect, dynamic registration, production minified bundle behavior, creative examples, playground isolation and a 1000-row performance smoke.

## Current limitations

- no SSR or hydration;
- no built-in async resource/suspense primitive;
- no built-in error-boundary component primitive;
- `{...}` expressions are property paths rather than arbitrary JavaScript;
- component scripts use `AsyncFunction`, so strict CSP requires an `unsafe-eval` allowance.

Do not silently claim these features exist.

## Rules for AI agents

When asked to create a Skein application:
1. Start with the smallest native HTML solution that satisfies the request.
2. Keep semantic and SEO-critical content outside dynamic components when it can be static.
3. Add Skein components only where interactivity/state is useful.
4. Prefer one-file `<template skein>` for tiny examples and prototypes.
5. Use `skein.min.js` for production/CDN examples.
6. Keep `{...}` bindings to paths; use `computed()` for derivation.
7. Use `.property`, `?boolean`, and `@event` with their intended DOM semantics.
8. Use stable keys for persistent list identity.
9. Use CSS for visual state and animation whenever possible.
10. Use native SVG and Canvas APIs directly.
11. Register cleanup with `abortSignal` or `onCleanup()`.
12. Do not add a framework, state library, templating library or editor library unless explicitly requested.
13. Do not resurrect removed pre-Skein APIs for compatibility.

When modifying the Skein runtime, read `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/skein/references/architecture.md`, relevant runtime source and tests before changing behavior.
